correctness.rationale: An exhaustive independent leaf-insertion checker enumerated 3,15,105,945 distinct rooted binary tree hypotheses, determined each rooted-triplet truth value from least common ancestor depths, and replayed complete binary strategies of depths 1,3,5,9 (1,7,31,511 internal query nodes) with nonempty leaves and exhaustive disjoint concept coverage. For 3,4,6, the respective hypothesis counts are below 2^(d+1). For n=5 the checker verifies for all 30 first queries that the 35-element positive branch has a unique possible 16/16-preserving split into 17 and 18, and the 17-child admits no 8/8 split, excluding depth six. A second recursive split generator agreed with leaf insertion at construction time.

value.rationale: The exact six-taxon online capacity nine saturates the nontrivial cardinality upper bound via a checkable 511-node adversarial strategy; the five-taxon failure at depth six identifies a contrasting sharp boundary. This separates adaptive online complexity from prior static phylogenetic flexibility, supplies reusable finite benchmark certificates, and concerns a natural rooted-triplet query language for phylogenetic reconstruction, not an arbitrary parameter slice. No general-size extrapolation is claimed.
